newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells dealers to buy sugar to boost reserves.
newsitem.headline: China tells dealers to buy sugar to boost reserves.

text.p: China's Ministry of Internal Trade has issued an urgent circular to government sugar firms nationwide to buy sugar to boost reserves, support output and stabilise the market, the China Business Daily said on Friday.

Officials said this week that the Chinese General Association of Light Industry planned to order government sugar companies to purchase between 200,000 and 400,000 tonnes of sugar to boost slumping domestic prices.
Sugar prices had slumped since the start of the crushing season in December, the newspaper said.
In the main southern, cane-producing region of Guangxi, prices had slipped to 3,750 yuan per tonne while the price in northern, beet-producing areas was about 4,100 yuan per tonne, it said.
That compared with about 3,780 yuan ($455) per tonne at the end of December, down from 4,150 yuan at the start of the month. Prices in December were about 200-300 yuan lower than a year ago.
The circular said sugar sales had slumped, with stockpiles rising in producing areas, resulting in big losses in revenue for sugar mills and farmers.
It ordered sugar companies to end their passive, wait-and-see attitude and to support local authorities and to buy in to increase the reserves, thus boosting prices.
China in 1996 began to order sugar mills in major producing areas to reserve sugar to boost prices to protect the domestic sugar industry, hit by huge imports and smuggling.

The Guangxi government had decided to purchase 100,000 tonnes before the Chinese Lunar New Year on February 7 at a minium purchase price of 3,800 yuan per tonne, state media has said. The regional government would purchase another 100,000 tonnes shortly after the holiday.
China expected to produce 6.6 million tonnes of sugar in the 1996/97 crushing season, the newspaper said.
China produced 8.4 million tonnes of sugar in 1996, up 13.15 percent from 1995/96, the State Statistical Bureau said.
